why: ADR-105 / task 581. The registry of stores in which a page's text counts as PERSISTED. `cytir.corpus.persisted` indexes exactly these and refuses to load a row whose page is in none of them. Globs, never file lists: the roster is derived from the storage tree at build time and printed with the result (corpus-doctrine 8). Paths are relative to AW_CORPUS_ROOT (pipeline/aw_paths.CORPUS_ROOT).

layer_meaning.l0: originals as fetched - raw response bytes. Re-extraction is local; ADR-026 calls this the only non-recomputable layer.
layer_meaning.l1: extracted documents - the FULL text/markdown of a page plus, where the lane recorded one, its sha. The ADR-105 bar.
layer_meaning.l2: passages - the chunked text a build consumed. Admits a page only under the ADR-093 overlap-chaining route (require='l1b'), never as a replay.

text_fields_note: A record counts as persistence only if one of `text_fields` is non-empty. Without that predicate the L1 release tree's `unresolved.jsonl.gz` - a list of URLs a lane FAILED to retrieve - would index as proof that those very pages are on disk (corpus-doctrine 3: our own failure is not the record's presence).
roster_note: The L1 release tree names its document files eleven different ways across 34 sources (l1-markdown-*.jsonl.gz, parents.jsonl.gz, gesetze.jsonl, legi.jsonl, pubmed-full.jsonl.gz, stages/markdown/data/*.jsonl.gz, lang=*/.multistream-fragments/range-*/shard-*.jsonl). A first draft of this file globbed `l1-markdown-*` and found EIGHT files in a tree of 156,704. The globs below are recursive over the whole layer for that reason; `tasks/581-scripts/store_discovery_581.py` is the exhaustive walk that established it.

stores.note: The gzipped half of the L1 document layer (51 files, ~56.9 GB at 2026-09-12): l1-markdown-*.jsonl.gz, parents.jsonl.gz, pubmed-full.jsonl.gz, legi-production-legal-markdown.jsonl.gz and the per-source stages/markdown/data trees. Task 579 measured this layer as THIN against L2 on deficit pages (median 0.77 of L2's words) - presence here is persistence, not completeness, and the completeness question was answered separately by the task-era script pipeline/page_text_completeness.py (retired in task 1939; pinned as git-blob:b4b5502901bab7824378c92b93a88581caf3fc59:pipeline/page_text_completeness.py). Neither guard substitutes for the other.

The uncompressed half (156,653 files, ~86.8 GB at 2026-09-12) - overwhelmingly wikipedia-markdown-v3's lang=*/.multistream-fragments/range-*/shard-*.jsonl. Excluded by every earlier glob and by far the largest L1 population.

pack_fetch.L0Store - raw response bytes, status, content_type, fetched_at, sha256. ADR-093 section 6 flagged that 16 of 28 waves carry sealed_by: None and three are gzip-corrupt at seal; the index build treats an unreadable shard as a FAILURE, not as an empty wave.
The wave1b direct-fetch raw HTML retained before the l0/ layout existed.

The corpus_store.py passage parquet - 78 waves, 159 files, 53,990,262 passages (task 407's exhaustive count, re-derived by task 579). This is production's OWN build input and the layer ADR-093's chainer reconstructs L1 from.
The n2-openalex passage wave, written in jsonl rather than parquet.
